customManagers.description: Versions pinned in Buckle vars, marked with a renovate comment
Git commits pinned in Buckle vars (follows a branch, updates the digest)

packageRules.description: Automerge digest, pin, patch and minor updates. A merge to main is a deploy: Buckle rolls it out to the fleet, canary first, and pauses on the first failed health check. Renovate merges itself (platformAutomerge off) because main has no required checks, so GitHub's automerge would not wait; Renovate waits for every check on the PR, buckle validate included.

Third-party software the fleet runs only once its release is three days old, so a broken release is usually yanked or fixed before it reaches a host: the pins in vars/ (custom regex) and the CLIs in mise.toml (Renovate's mise manager), so a CLI never runs ahead of the fleet's pin. Not for the user's own projects below.
Own projects (released on purpose, wanted right away): no waiting.
Majors automerge too (nobody approves by hand), but only once the release is a week old: time for a broken major to be fixed or yanked. Buckle majors stay disabled below.
k3s: minors apart from patches (and +k3sN rebuilds), one minor per PR, because Kubernetes can't skip a minor. Patches automerge like everything else; minors follow the next rule.

k3s minors are cluster upgrades and must not skip a minor. They automerge one at a time: validate.yml fails a PR that moves k3s_version by more than one minor from main (the next minor's PR passes once the previous one merged and Renovate rebased it), and only on Monday mornings, so each upgrade has a week to roll out before the next.

Buckle: the fleet's pin (vars/versions.yaml) and the CLI (mise.toml, which Renovate's mise manager names github:SierraSoftworks/buckle) in one PR, so CI validates with the binary the fleet gets; validate.yml runs it on an x86-64-v2 CPU like the NUC's, which catches a release the NUC can't run (2.14.0 crashed it with SIGILL). Without the second name, 2.22.2 reached mise.toml alone and left the fleet on 2.22.0 (2026-11-26). Majors stay off: the canary blades' agents would upgrade before the server, and a protocol break there takes the control plane down.
compute-blade-agent: agent on the blades (vars/versions.yaml) and bladectl here (mise.toml, through the mise manager) in one PR
